Title: Boulder City Council Meeting - 9-28-23 (Study Session: Municipal Court Update, Police Department Update, Homelessness Programs Update)

Topic1.Title: Municipal Court Overview and Community Court Model
Topic1.Summary: Judge Khan presented the court's problem-solving philosophy, administrative and staffing changes, and the new state live-streaming requirement. He described the FastTrack process for quality-of-life violations, typical outcomes such as deferred adjudication and restorative justice programs, and the limits of jail sentencing due to jail capacity and 48-hour bond rules. Council members asked how cases are assigned to Community Court, and staff agreed to provide written criteria and data in a future hotline post. Judge Khan also noted that housing has been shown to reduce recidivism among high utilizers.

Topic2.Title: Police Department Crime Trends and Significant Incidents
Topic2.Summary: Chief Harold reported that violent crime and property crime have both increased since 2019, driven by simple and aggravated assaults, menacing, and personal and business thefts, while motor vehicle theft is down 48% since 2020. Drug and narcotics violations rose 79% from last year, with overdoses concentrated in downtown and University Hill neighborhoods. Deputy Chief Redfern reviewed significant incidents, including a fatal officer-involved shooting, a child homicide, a stabbing outside the municipal building, and a vehicle attack in Central Park, and highlighted community engagement events. Council discussed jail overcrowding, the need for more mental health and addiction services, and possible increases in human trafficking and hate crimes.

Topic3.Title: Homelessness Programs, Services, and Alternative Sheltering
Topic3.Summary: Megan Newton and Kurt Fehab presented a summer point-in-time count showing stable unsheltered and sheltered numbers, along with new programs including local vouchers, Building Home peer and retention services, the Rest Fit Center, Project Recovery and Tribe, the Boulder Community Health high utilizer program, and the day services center plans. They reviewed housing exits averaging 25 per month, prevention efforts, racial equity data, and the 2024 budget of about $11.6 million. Staff presented options and cost estimates for safe outdoor spaces and alternative sheltering, emphasizing that wraparound services and infrastructure are essential. Council expressed mixed views, with several members supporting further exploration of additional shelter capacity, and the matter was referred to a future council decision with budget implications considered.
